code_quality.title: Split large admin page files into smaller components
code_quality.description: Multiple admin and dashboard pages exceed 700-1000+ lines, combining data fetching, state management, form handling, list rendering, and modal logic in single files. Files like plans/page.tsx (1086 lines), overrides/page.tsx (977 lines), ai/page.tsx (919 lines), organizations/page.tsx (811 lines), and tables/page.tsx (744 lines) are far too large for maintainability.
code_quality.rationale: Files over 500 lines significantly increase cognitive load, make code reviews difficult, and create merge conflicts. Large monolithic components are harder to test in isolation and violate single responsibility principle. Splitting into focused components enables better code reuse and faster development.
code_quality.currentState: Single large page files containing all state management, data fetching, rendering logic, and multiple modals (e.g., plans/page.tsx has 1086 lines handling Plans tab, Features tab, plan modals, feature modals, and plan-feature assignment modals)
code_quality.proposedChange:
Extract into smaller focused components:
1. Create components/admin/plans/ folder with: PlansList.tsx, FeaturesTab.tsx, PlanModal.tsx, FeatureModal.tsx, PlanFeaturesModal.tsx
2. Create components/dashboard/tables/ with: TablesList.tsx, TableItem.tsx, TableModal.tsx, QRCodeModal.tsx
3. Move shared state patterns into custom hooks (usePlansCRUD, useTablesCRUD)
4. Keep page.tsx files under 200 lines as container components
code_quality.bestPractice: Component files should ideally be under 300 lines. Container components handle orchestration while presentational components handle rendering.
prerequisites: Create shared component architecture in components/ folder

code_quality.title: Extract duplicated CRUD state management into reusable hooks
code_quality.description: Nearly identical state management patterns are repeated across 19+ page components with 204 occurrences of setIsLoading/setError/setIsSaving calls. Each CRUD page duplicates: loading state, error state, saving state, modal open/close state, form data state, delete confirmation state, and their associated handlers.
code_quality.rationale: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) violation leads to inconsistent behavior, more bugs, and increased maintenance burden. When a bug is found in one pattern, it must be fixed in 19 places. Extracting to custom hooks enables consistent error handling, loading states, and optimistic updates across the application.
code_quality.currentState:
Each page independently declares and manages:
- const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true)
- const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
- const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = useState(false)
- const [isModalOpen, setIsModalOpen] = useState(false)
- const [editingItem, setEditingItem] = useState(null)
- const [deleteTarget, setDeleteTarget] = useState(null)
- fetchData(), handleSubmit(), handleDelete() functions with similar try/catch patterns
code_quality.proposedChange:
Create hooks/useCRUD.ts with generic CRUD operations:
1. useCRUD<T>(tableName, options) - handles fetch, create, update, delete
2. useFormModal<T>() - handles modal state, form data, validation
3. useDeleteConfirmation<T>() - handles delete confirmation flow
4. useAsyncOperation() - handles loading/error/success states
code_quality.bestPractice: Custom hooks should encapsulate reusable stateful logic. Generic CRUD hooks reduce boilerplate and ensure consistent UX patterns.
prerequisites: Add unit tests for the new hooks

code_quality.title: Create reusable icon component system
code_quality.description: 175 inline SVG icons are scattered across 19 files with duplicate icon definitions. Icons like edit, delete, plus, check, eye, eye-off, and loading spinner are copy-pasted repeatedly with inconsistent sizing (h-4 w-4, h-5 w-5, h-6 w-6) and stroke widths.
code_quality.rationale: Inline SVG duplication increases bundle size, makes icon updates tedious (must change in multiple places), and leads to visual inconsistency. A centralized icon system enables consistent iconography, easier theming, and potential tree-shaking optimizations.
code_quality.currentState:
SVG icons are embedded inline with varying sizes:
<svg className="h-4 w-4" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" stroke="currentColor" strokeWidth={2}>
  <path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" d="M11 5H6a2 2 0 00-2 2v11..." />
</svg>
(This edit icon pattern appears 15+ times with slight variations)
code_quality.proposedChange:
Create components/ui/icons/ with:
1. Icon.tsx - base wrapper component with size prop ('sm' | 'md' | 'lg')
2. icons/index.ts - barrel export of all icons
3. Individual icon files or icon sprite
Alternatively, adopt lucide-react or heroicons library which are already compatible with the existing icon style

code_quality.title: Extract shared alert/notification component
code_quality.description: Error alert pattern is duplicated 36 times across 19 files with nearly identical JSX structure for displaying error messages. Each file has its own implementation of the red-bordered error box with dismiss button.
code_quality.rationale: UI consistency is compromised when the same pattern is implemented differently across files. If the design team wants to update error styling, 36 files must be modified. A shared Alert component also enables adding features like auto-dismiss, different severity levels, and accessibility improvements in one place.
code_quality.currentState:
Error display pattern copied across files: {error && (
{error}
)}
code_quality.proposedChange:
Create components/ui/alert.tsx with variants:
- Alert component with props: variant ('error' | 'warning' | 'success' | 'info'), dismissible, onDismiss
- Support for title + description
- Auto-dismiss timeout option
- Toast notification variant for transient messages
code_quality.bestPractice: UI patterns should be implemented once as reusable components. Alert/notification components should follow WAI-ARIA guidelines.

code_quality.title: Add unit test coverage for dashboard page components
code_quality.description: While integration tests exist (19 test files), the dashboard and admin page components have no unit tests. The products, categories, tables, and plans pages contain complex business logic for CRUD operations, form validation, and state management that should be tested in isolation.
code_quality.rationale: Unit tests provide faster feedback than integration tests and help document expected component behavior. Testing hooks and utility functions in isolation catches bugs earlier in development. Current test coverage focuses on integration flows but misses edge cases in individual components.
